nodes.label: Adapter
nodes.rationale: In loom, a **harness adapter**: the module that maps loom's generic content (skills, agents, workflow) onto a specific [Harness](#harness)'s native config format. It owns the harness-specific knowledge so the [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) entrypoint and the [Setup contract](#setup-contract) stay harness-agnostic. Supporting a new harness = adding an adapter under `adapters/<harness>/`, not modifying loom's core content.

nodes.label: ADR (Architecture Decision Record)
nodes.rationale: A document that records a significant architectural decision, its context, and consequences. ADRs live in `agent/wiki/adr/`.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.rationale: An autonomous entity with a clear identity and bounded responsibility. Agents specialize by problem domain, not technology.

nodes.label: Altitude
nodes.rationale: The scale at which planning and coordination happen. loom distinguishes two. The **micro** altitude is a single [SDLC](workflows/sdlc/index.md) run — one shaped change flowing Planning → Implementation → Verification, coordinating in harness memory. The **macro** altitude is project management *above* one run — a [Resident agent](#resident-agent) charting many efforts as nested [wayfinder](SKILLS/planning/wayfinder/SKILL.md) maps and dispatching their leaves *into* SDLC runs. The two altitudes m

nodes.label: Altitude seam
nodes.rationale: The boundary between the macro and micro [Altitudes](#altitude), and the **translator** that crosses it. A [Resident agent](#resident-agent) performs two translations, reusing the existing [Seam Artifact Protocol](wiki/patterns/seam-artifact-protocol.md) PRODUCE/DISCOVER contract across the boundary: **down** — a macro tracker ticket plus its linked artifacts becomes a `shaping/<milestone>/` [Seam artifact](#seam-artifact) in the SDLC run's memory [Ledger](#ledger), which Planning's DISCOVER gat

nodes.label: Artifact ref
nodes.rationale: The second instrument of the networked [Substrate](#substrate) class ([ADR-022](wiki/adr/adr-022-reachable-artifact-substrate.md)): a git ref on the server — an **orphan branch per effort** (`loom-artifacts/<map-slug>`, disconnected history so it never tangles a rebase or merge of `main`) — that holds a HITL ticket's **bulky content** (a `grilling` design doc, a `prototype`'s output, `research` findings), fetched by URL on demand and never checked into a working tree. Where the **tracker/board**

nodes.label: Board
nodes.rationale: The set of issues **reachable from a `wayfinder:map` via `blocking` edges** ([ADR-029](wiki/adr/adr-029-single-edge-board-graph.md)) — not simply "the repo's issues". An issue outside that reachable set is [Unmapped](#unmapped), never a board member, regardless of its open/ closed state. [Takeable](#takeable) and [Frontier](#frontier) are computed only over board members; mere presence in the repo's issue list confers nothing.

nodes.label: Board API
nodes.rationale: The **deterministic interface to the macro source-of-truth board** — a small distributable the harness installs (initially a thin wrapper over `gh` for plain GitHub Issues + native issue dependencies), exposing a tiny stable verb set the [macro tick](#manual-tick) invokes, namespaced under `loom`: `loom board read [--frontier]`, `loom board tree`, `loom board apply <ticket> <transition>`, and `loom board reconcile` (see [Board reconcile](#board-reconcile)). Its purpose is to move board **mutatio

nodes.label: Board member
nodes.rationale: A `wayfinder:map`, or a ticket whose `blocking` chain reaches one ([ADR-029](wiki/adr/adr-029-single-edge-board-graph.md)). Membership is an **edge property, not a status** — it survives closure, so a closed ticket stays a member and keeps counting toward its map's completion. Replaces the `parent`/`subIssues` sub-issue nesting ADR-025 §6 used for grouping (no 7-level nesting cap, no BFS).

nodes.label: Board reconcile
nodes.rationale: The **one idempotent detect-drift → repair operation** of the [Board API](#board-api), invoked at both ends of a [manual tick](#manual-tick): once *before* the tick reads (step 0), so the tick acts on truth, and again *before* exit (final step), repairing drift the tick itself introduced — the same command at both ends, so the human's standalone "fix the board" run is that same command. Drift (e.g. an `sdlc:in-progress` leaf whose SDLC run already wrote its verified-change) therefore survives at

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.rationale: A generic, harness-agnostic power an [Agent](#agent) may hold: `read`, `edit`, `shell`, `delegate`, `persist`, `interview`, `web`, `docs-lookup`, `tasks`. Capabilities are named independently of any tool; each [Adapter](#adapter) maps them onto its [Harness](#harness)'s concrete tool names — and tolerates deviation when a harness's names differ (a mapping the adapter discovers or is told, never hardcodes blindly).

nodes.label: Communication protocol document
nodes.rationale: A dedicated, standalone per-project document stating where that project's [Ledger](#ledger) lives, its namespace convention, and each [Stage](#stage)'s expected [Seam artifacts](#seam-artifact). It is separate from per-project context ([AGENTS.md](#adapter)) and from any single agent or skill: it is the shared contract they all point at. Agents and skills that participate in handoff **reference** it rather than re-deriving the convention. Each [Adapter](#adapter) concretizes it in the harness's

nodes.label: Context-First
nodes.rationale: Design philosophy that treats context as a first-class resource. Minimize what enters context, maximize signal-to-noise.

nodes.label: Core
nodes.rationale: The essential, minimal implementation. Everything else is built on top of core.

nodes.label: Criterion type
nodes.rationale: One of `artifact` | `executable` | `judgment` — the tag on a [Gate](#gate) criterion that determines who checks it and whether it may be bypassed. A bypassed criterion is logged on the tracker, never silently.

nodes.label: Deep Module
nodes.rationale: A module with a small interface and deep implementation. Hides complexity from callers.

nodes.label: Dispatcher
nodes.rationale: A [Role](#role) that holds the `delegate` [Capability](#capability): it routes work to other agents rather than doing it itself. Dispatchers typically **withhold `edit`**, which forces them to delegate instead of quietly doing the work in-place. The [Orchestrator](#orchestrator) is the canonical dispatcher; **Shaping** is a second, *read-only* one — it dispatches recon and research to the `explore` utility and spikes to `quick`/`deep` while staying `edit`-free ([ADR-021](wiki/adr/adr-021-shaping

nodes.label: Dogfood
nodes.rationale: To use your own tools and systems. "Eating your own dogfood" means the framework uses its own principles and patterns.

nodes.label: Domain-specialized utility
nodes.rationale: A [Utility (dispatched) agent](#utility-dispatched-agent) scoped to a **problem domain** (e.g. frontend) rather than an **intelligence tier** (`quick`/`deep`). It wires that domain's skill cluster and is dispatched for work in that domain. This closes the gap between the tier-based roster and the wisdom principle *"specialize by problem domain, not technology"* — the tier utilities are difficulty-shaped; a domain-specialized utility is domain-shaped.

nodes.label: Evidence producer
nodes.rationale: The command or distinct actor that grounds a [Gate](#gate) criterion. A criterion without one is self-attestation — the agent that did the work declaring it acceptable, which is exactly what a Gate exists to rule out.

nodes.label: Form slop
nodes.rationale: An agent leaves required paperwork undone — an artifact left unwritten, a field missing, a gate left unrun, a board left stale. Caught by the [Gate](#gate): an `artifact` or `executable` criterion fails instead of being self-attested.

nodes.label: Frontier
nodes.rationale: The set of every [Takeable](#takeable) issue on the board at a given moment ([ADR-029](wiki/adr/adr-029-single-edge-board-graph.md)) — a computed *state*, not a fixed membership; it is exactly as volatile as the board's edges and assignments. Exposed via `loom board read --frontier`. A specific snapshot (e.g. "today it's a single issue") is a transient board state, never part of this term's meaning — what qualifies is defined entirely by [Takeable](#takeable).

nodes.label: Gate
nodes.rationale: An ordered set of typed criteria, committed per project, where every criterion names its [evidence producer](#evidence-producer) or is marked judgment and escalated to a different actor. Distinguished from *exit criteria*, which assert an outcome with nothing able to refute it — a Gate fails loudly at a known exit code instead of passing silently.

nodes.label: Graduation
nodes.rationale: A [Mechanism](#mechanism)'s promotion path: skill-local → shared distributable (once a second caller needs it) → structural withhold, where the check disappears because the failure it guarded against becomes impossible (e.g. a role with no `edit` capability cannot commit a bad edit). The end state of graduation is *fewer* mechanisms, not more.

nodes.label: Harness
nodes.rationale: The agent tool a project runs in — the thing that reads customization files and drives the model (Mirai, Claude Code, Cursor, Aider, OpenCode, …). Each harness stores its customization (instructions, agents, skills, prompts, hooks) in its own **native format** and location. loom is harness-agnostic; a [Harness Adapter](#adapter) is what teaches loom a given harness's format.

nodes.label: Invocation surface
nodes.rationale: The set of entry points that may **start** a [Role](#role) — a facet of the role parallel to its [Capability](#capability) set. Where the capability set answers *what the role may do*, the invocation surface answers *who may start it*: a **human** (the harness's agent picker / UI front door) or **another agent** (subagent dispatch). loom names two surfaces:

nodes.label: Judgment slop
nodes.rationale: An agent evaluates a tradeoff badly. Irreducible — no amount of additional prose prevents it. Answered structurally by producer ≠ judge (the actor that reviews is not the actor that did the work), never by more prose.

nodes.label: Ledger
nodes.rationale: The durable store for [Seam artifacts](#seam-artifact). Its root resolves through the [`persist`](#capability) capability (harness-agnostic); artifacts are addressed by `<ledger-root>/<stage>/<milestone-slug>/*.md` and indexed by a **manifest** at `<ledger-root>/index.md` (milestone, stage, artifact, status, updated — latest row wins). A producing agent writes and registers; a receiving agent reads the manifest and loads the latest artifact for its seam. The concrete substrate (harness memory /

nodes.label: Lifecycle Bucket
nodes.rationale: A grouping of related tasks or concerns that share a lifecycle. Helps organize work by phase.

nodes.label: Manual tick
nodes.rationale: A single execution of the macro-PM [tick loop](workflows/macro-pm/index.md#the-tick-loop) run **on demand by a human or per-invocation harness**, rather than by a [Resident agent](#resident-agent)'s `cron`/`gateway`. Because the tick is harness-agnostic prose over a [Board API](#board-api), the same loop runs unchanged whether a resident daemon fires it on an interval or a person triggers it once (e.g. a Mirai custom agent invoked by hand) — the clearest proof the tick is *prose + a board script

nodes.label: Mechanism
nodes.rationale: A script that removes a class of failure by [re-executing reality](#re-executing-reality) rather than describing it. Only trustworthy once observed failing (`verified-failing`) — a mechanism nobody has watched catch a real failure is unproven.

nodes.label: Membership edge
nodes.rationale: The edge shape `ticket → map`: a ticket `blocks` its map exactly as it would block another ticket ([ADR-029](wiki/adr/adr-029-single-edge-board-graph.md)), so **a map is not done until every ticket blocking it is**. Distinguished from an [Ordering edge](#ordering-edge) only by whether the far node's type is `wayfinder:map` — both are the same native GitHub dependency mechanism, read differently depending on the node it points at. Replaces `parent`/`subIssues` entirely.

nodes.label: Orchestrator
nodes.rationale: An agent [Role](#role) that runs the Implementation loop: it gauges each task's size and **dispatches it to the correct implementation-agent class** (high / mid / low intelligence) to maximize the chance of a successful implementation. It does not rely on a small agent self-assessing its own capability. The Orchestrator also enforces the architecture-prerequisite gate.

nodes.label: Ordering edge
nodes.rationale: The edge shape `ticket → ticket`: a real dependency between two non-map tickets ([ADR-029](wiki/adr/adr-029-single-edge-board-graph.md)), holding [Takeable](#takeable) closed until it resolves. Same native GitHub issue-dependency mechanism as a [Membership edge](#membership-edge) — the only difference is that the far node is not a `wayfinder:map`.

nodes.label: Plugin
nodes.rationale: An extension point that allows external code to hook into a system. Plugins extend behavior without modifying core.

nodes.label: Quality aspect
nodes.rationale: One of the four distinct dimensions a [quality baseline](#quality-baseline) covers: **lint** (style/mechanical correctness), **code-quality** (complexity/duplication/maintainability), **security** (SAST + vulnerable dependencies), and **coverage** (test %). Each aspect names its own tool and floor; an aspect with no keyless tool for the stack is recorded as `none` with a reason.

nodes.label: Quality baseline
nodes.rationale: A per-project quality floor recorded at [setup](#setup-contract) and re-checked at every [quality gate](workflows/sdlc/implementation.md#quality-gates)'s Verify step. It names one tool + run command + floor per [quality aspect](#quality-aspect), defaults to a **ratchet** (no-regression) floor, is built from **keyless-first** tools, and lives in a single source of truth (the project's committed tool config when present, else a loom-owned section in the project-context file). A metric dropping bel

nodes.label: Ratchet
nodes.rationale: The loop that converts a recall failure into a [Mechanism](#mechanism) on its first occurrence, so a lesson stops enlarging the prose an agent must recall. Named for the no-regression floor pattern in [quality baseline](#quality-baseline), generalized here to any forgotten environment fact.

nodes.label: Re-executing reality
nodes.rationale: The property separating a trustworthy executable check from a decorative one: the check runs the real toolchain and reads its actual result, rather than reading a description of what the result should be. What a [Mechanism](#mechanism) does to catch [recall slop](#recall-slop).

nodes.label: Recall slop
nodes.rationale: An agent reasons correctly but forgets a known environment fact or precondition — the tell is that the system already knew the answer. Fully mechanizable, unlike judgment slop; caught by a [Mechanism](#mechanism) rather than more prose, and ratcheted on first occurrence because a forgotten fact will always recur.

nodes.label: Resident agent
nodes.rationale: A memory-bearing agent that runs the macro [Altitude](#altitude) as a **reactive worker** over a [Networked substrate](#substrate) (e.g. watching a tracker/board, potentially unattended). The **board is the single source of truth**: the agent's private memory holds only non-load-bearing continuity — persona, user preferences, learned skills, conversation continuity — and **never** project state, so a fresh instance on another server reconstructs the project from the board alone. Its routing is *

nodes.label: Role
nodes.rationale: An [Agent](#agent) defined by its **scoped set of [Capabilities](#capability)** — what it is allowed to do — rather than only by its problem domain. The role *is* the capability grant: change the grant and you change the role. Enforcement lives in the grant, not in prose asking the agent to behave.

nodes.label: RPI (Research → Plan → Implement)
nodes.rationale: Disciplined workflow for complex tasks.

nodes.label: Seam artifact
nodes.rationale: The document that crosses a [Stage](#stage) boundary — the baton one stage's owner hands to the next. Shaping emits a milestone with design docs (findings, domain model, design decisions); Delivery emits a shipped, verified change with its acceptance evidence; Closing emits durable, curated knowledge. A seam artifact carries the *connective tissue* the next agent needs — it **references** PRDs, plans, ADRs, commits, and diffs by path or URL rather than re-embedding them. The [Seam Artifact Proto

nodes.label: Setup contract
nodes.rationale: The universal, harness-agnostic flow every [Adapter](#adapter) implements to install loom into a project: **explore → interview → present & confirm → generate (in the harness's native format) → verify**. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) defines the contract; each adapter supplies the harness-specific "generate" and "verify" steps. Interview-driven, not a mechanical copy — the interview tailors which skills/agents/stages the project needs.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.rationale: A reusable judgment pattern. Not just "how" but "when" and "why". A skill encodes decision-making logic that can be applied across multiple contexts.

nodes.label: Stage
nodes.rationale: An ownership grouping of [Workflow](#workflow) phases that marks a real handoff **seam** — the point where ownership changes hands. The SDLC workflow has three: **Shaping** (Discovery+Design), **Delivery** (Planning+Implementation+Verification), and **Closing** (Preservation). Stages carry no gates of their own; they name *who* owns the work and *what* [Seam artifact](#seam-artifact) crosses each seam.

nodes.label: Substrate
nodes.rationale: Where a [Ledger](#ledger)'s bytes actually land — chosen per project (and, per [ADR-018](wiki/adr/adr-018-macro-project-management.md), per [Altitude](#altitude)) at [setup](#setup-contract), never hardcoded by the protocol. Three classes: **harness memory** (survives across conversations, fast — but not git-committed, so it does not distribute across agents on different servers); a **committed repo folder** (harness-neutral, reviewable — but adds state files to the code tree); and a **networked

nodes.label: Takeable
nodes.rationale: The five-conjunct predicate `member ∧ type ≠ map ∧ open ∧ no open blocker ∧ unassigned` ([ADR-029](wiki/adr/adr-029-single-edge-board-graph.md), decision D1) — corrected from ADR-025 §8's three-conjunct `(open ∧ unblocked ∧ unassigned)`, which over-collected to 9 items on the live board including the map itself. The `member` conjunct excludes [Unmapped](#unmapped) issues; `type ≠ map` is kept as an explicit guard even though [Board member](#board-member)ship already makes a map non-takeable (a m

nodes.label: Unmapped
nodes.rationale: Open, and **not** a [Board member](#board-member) — an issue awaiting triage, never auto-typed into membership ([ADR-029](wiki/adr/adr-029-single-edge-board-graph.md)). Surfaced only via `loom board read --unmapped`, kept out of the default `read` payload so an untriaged issue never silently joins a map's [Frontier](#frontier). `Board reconcile` never repairs this state itself — typing a ticket stays a human judgment call.

nodes.label: Utility (dispatched) agent
nodes.rationale: A [Role](#role) that **receives** dispatched work — it holds execution [Capabilities](#capability) (`edit`, `shell`) but not `delegate` as its purpose. Utility agents are the reusable executor/verifier pool a [Dispatcher](#dispatcher) hands tasks to: `explore` (read-only recon), `quick` (mechanical edits), `deep` (hard problems), and the Verifier (checks an artifact against its acceptance criteria, `edit`-free so it verifies rather than fixes).

nodes.label: Verification Culture
nodes.rationale: The principle carrying the **iron law**: *no completion, success, or positive work-state claim without fresh verification evidence, gathered in the same turn it is claimed.* It binds not just "done" but every paraphrase or implication of success. Harness-agnostic — it names *evidence*, never a specific command; the [verification-before-completion](SKILLS/verification/verification-before-completion/SKILL.md) skill is the *procedure* that operationalizes it.

nodes.label: Wiki
nodes.rationale: Centralized knowledge repository. Contains principles, patterns, and environments. Reference material, not procedures. Terminology lives in this file (`CONTEXT.md`), not in the wiki.

nodes.label: Workflow
nodes.rationale: An ordered orchestration document for a specific lifecycle. A workflow is **prose-first**: it describes phases, gates, recommended skills, and policies as guidance for an interpreting agent — not as a machine-parseable contract. It is a **seed** an [Adapter](#adapter) compiles into a concrete harness (agent configs, skill wiring, commands) for a target tool. Distinct from a [Skill](#skill) (single judgment pattern) and an [Agent](#agent) (identity wiring skills).

nodes.label: Wrapper
nodes.rationale: A function or class that adds behavior around an existing function or class. Wrappers are composable.

Jacquard
nodes.rationale: Named after the Jacquard loom, which took the pattern out of the weaver's head and put it on punched cards the machine could read while the weaver still worked the loom — chosen as the name because it captures a project's theory written where machines can read it, with a human still at the loom.

nodes.label: Humans decide, agents do, checks verify
Written and checked beats smarter
nodes.rationale: A model should never have to infer what the project could have written down, or reason about what a script could check; better context lets the project use a smaller, cheaper, more local model. Scaffolding that only props up a weak model is temporary by design — written/checked project knowledge is not, because no model recovers an undocumented decision or an unrun test.

nodes.label: Autonomy is earned by checks
nodes.rationale: An agent acts alone exactly where a check can catch it being wrong; where nothing can, a human decides. A mistake a check could have caught becomes a check the first time it happens, moving human attention toward decisions over time, but autonomy never reaches full automation — judgment doesn't automate away and accountability stays human. Semi-automated is the design, not a step toward full automation.

nodes.label: Humans keep the theory
nodes.rationale: Jacquard is built as if no human writes the code — a forcing function, not a forecast: every gap a human would patch by hand must instead be closed in the harness. The human's remaining work is the project's theory (purpose, decisions, vocabulary, definition of good), kept where agents can read it; keeping that theory is also what keeps a human able to judge work they no longer type.

nodes.label: Knowledge lives in the project
nodes.rationale: Knowledge must live in the project itself, never inside a model, vendor, or runtime, so it outlives all three — written once, kept current, checked, so a fresh agent anywhere can rebuild the whole picture from it.

nodes.label: Graph freshness check
nodes.rationale: Nothing gates the graph query path on staleness, and graphify's rebuild hook only watches code changes, which this prose corpus has almost none of — so a graph can be many commits behind and will not say so. Must diff changed markdown files since built_at_commit and read those directly instead of trusting the graph; whoever changed them owed the graph a regeneration.

nodes.label: Stranded file
nodes.rationale: A stranded file is one that does not trace back to VISION.md (CONSTITUTION.md rule 5). Known stranded files are listed in .claude/hooks/validate-baseline.txt and reviewed one at a time.

nodes.label: built_at_commit (graph freshness stamp)
nodes.rationale: The merge stamps built_at_commit with HEAD, so a change must be committed first, then the graph regenerated and committed — extracting before the commit leaves the just-changed files reading as stale.

nodes.label: SPEC.md — loom Agent Framework Conformance Rules
Progressive disclosure (wiki roots summarize, leaves hold detail)
Research dated pages (OKF v0.2 trust/lifecycle dates)
nodes.rationale: stale_after is listed as advisory only and never blocks the gate, because the calendar alone must not break the gate — only a missing/malformed date block does.

nodes.label: Cross-linking convention (relative paths from agent/ root)
Lifecycle bucket definitions (discovery, design, planning, implementation, verification, preservation, meta)
User-invoked wrapper vs model-invoked core (mattpocock split)
nodes.rationale: Wrappers set context and surface output; cores define reusable procedures without a user-facing trigger. A core SKILL.md must include 'model-invoked' or 'core primitive' in its description so validators can identify it mechanically.

nodes.label: Adapter (extension point / adapter contract)
nodes.rationale: The adapter layer shipped as a prose contract in contract/ rather than the tooling design (loom.toml, a Rust/TypeScript distribution binary) originally explored in ADR-001 — that design space is superseded in practice by ADR-005 and ADR-013, kept only as historical record.

nodes.label: Path-flexibility preamble (loom.toml > framework default > legacy fallback)
Setup contract (five-step: explore, interview, present & confirm, generate, verify)
nodes.rationale: The interview step is not optional — a mechanical copy is non-conformant. Harness-specific knowledge must stay under adapters/<harness>/ and never leak into SETUP.md; the generic contract body lives once in contract/ and adapters must reference, never restate, it.

nodes.label: Mirai delivery conformance
nodes.rationale: loom's first concrete adapter — the first implementation of the harness-agnostic setup contract.

nodes.label: OpenCode delivery conformance
nodes.rationale: OpenCode's seam obligation is a local-only, blanket-gitignored .loom/handoffs/ ledger — protocol document, manifest, and artifacts all under .loom/**, never committed — because OpenCode has no memory tool or handoffs: primitive. Per-role tiering is expressed directly by each agent's inline model: field, so loom renders no external model-tiering overlay (ADR-014).

nodes.label: Hermes delivery conformance
nodes.rationale: Hermes is loom's first resident-archetype adapter: profile-home-centric, delivered as a git-committable profile distribution plus the project's AGENTS.md. The micro SDLC ledger cannot be Hermes memory because the dispatched SDLC run executes in a separate harness process and memory does not cross a harness boundary. The macro-PM resident lifecycle is the whole point of this adapter; a single terminating SDLC effort belongs on a per-invocation harness (Mirai/OpenCode), not Hermes.

nodes.label: Altitude (two altitude-scoped substrates: macro board tracker vs micro SDLC ledger)
nodes.rationale: A networked tracker over MCP serves the macro board; a shared, on-disk, gitignored directory serves the micro SDLC ledger. The split exists because memory does not cross a harness boundary — the dispatched SDLC run executes in a separate harness process from the resident macro-PM.

nodes.label: REGISTRY.md mechanism ledger (owner / grounds / earned-by / verified-failing)
nodes.rationale: Every gate mechanism must show a verified-failing case — falsifiability evidence that the check once genuinely failed before being fixed — not just a passing run. Example: scripts/validate.sh pre-fix reported '0 validated / 0 checked, all OK, exit 0' on a renamed working-tree copy, because a root-resolution + skills/ casing bug masked every count; post-fix it correctly exits 1 on an empty adapter dir or hidden SKILLS/.
